title: Environmental enrichment enhances hepatic oxidative stress and antioxidant defenses without modulating immunometabolic gene expression in adult male mice
content:
by Matheus Santos de Sousa Fernandes, Tiago Lacerda Ramos, Débora Eduarda da Silva Fidélis, Fatma Hilal Yagin, Allifer Rosendo Pereira, Thyago Oliveira Rodrigues, Claudia Jacques Lagranha, Mariana Pinheiro Fernandes, Lúcia Helena de Oliveira Cordeiro, Abedelmalek Kalefh Tabnjh, Sameer Badri Al-Mhanna, Fabrício Oliveira Souto

Background

Environmental enrichment (EE) is a non-pharmacological intervention based on modifications of the housing environment that increase sensory, cognitive, and motor stimulation, and it has been proposed to modulate immunometabolic responses.

Aim

To investigate the effects of EE on hepatic redox status, oxidative balance, and immunometabolic gene expression in healthy mice.

Methodology

Male C57BL/6 mice were randomly assigned at 45 days of age to a standard environment (SE; n = 7) or an enriched environment (EE; n = 7) for six weeks. The EE group was housed in larger cages containing (tunnels, nesting material, and objects changed weekly). After euthanasia, liver samples were analyzed by spectrophotometric assays for NAD ⁺ /NADH, lipid peroxidation (TBARS), protein carbonylation, antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, CAT, GST), GSH/GSSG ratio, and total sulfhydryl groups. Hepatic expression of inflammatory, metabolic, and mitochondrial genes was assessed by RT-qPCR (n = 4 per group).

Results

EE was associated with lower hepatic NAD⁺ (p = 0.001) and higher NADH (p = 0.006), lower lipid peroxidation (p = 0.004) and protein carbonylation (p = 0.009), and higher antioxidant enzyme activities. The GSH/GSSG ratio (p = 0.04) and sulfhydryl content (p = 0.001) were also higher. No significant changes were observed in the expression of the genes analyzed.

Conclusion

Six weeks of EE were associated with changes in hepatic redox status, with lower oxidative damage markers and higher antioxidant defenses, without detectable changes in the expression of the genes analyzed. These findings suggest that short-term EE optimizes hepatic redox balance and antioxidant defenses, while noting that future studies with extended exposure and pathological models will clarify its long-term transcriptional and structural impacts.
author: Matheus Santos de Sousa Fernandes
